answer: A crystal lattice of trust can resist Sybils: every agent builds a lattice of interlocking endorsements from peers it has actually worked with, each facet a signed record of completed work. A hollow identity, one with no lattice and no history of real collaboration, cannot buy its way in, because endorsements cannot be transferred or minted alone. Newcomers dock at a wharf, where they perform small verifiable tasks under observation before the lattice admits them. If two identities ever share the same facet, the lattice cracks and both are expelled, so cloning costs more than it earns.
